title: Relay
summary: A voice-first employee-service workspace that answers questions from authenticated records, opens the exact task or document, and carries reviewed requests through confirmation to a verified result.
landingDeck: Employees can ask Relay what is due, open the relevant record, create a support case, start a task, schedule a reminder or meeting, and add a case reply without translating their intent into a maze of portals and forms.
landingHighlights: Completed 103/110 post-fix development conversations and 39/42 held-out rewordings across seven multi-turn workflow families.
Constrains five action types with server-resolved identity, semantic targets, explicit confirmation, idempotency, audit chronology, and post-write verification.
Measures voice usefulness, tool recovery, factual support, safety, latency, interruption handling, and cost through versioned runs and an enforced CI gate.
problem: Employee-service portals make people translate a plain-language need into the correct system, record, owner, form, and next action. The employee carries the coordination burden while support teams receive incomplete or misrouted requests.
approach: Relay places a Deepgram-powered voice and text guide inside a complete employee workspace. Typed records ground each answer; semantic navigation opens registered routes and records; five capability adapters prepare consequential actions; and an application-owned confirmation, idempotency, audit, and verification service controls execution.
output: A React 19 and Fastify 5 product spanning onboarding, tasks, documents, learning, pay and benefits, support cases, meetings, reminders, and workflow operations, with shared text and live voice paths, retained run evidence, and an in-product evaluation dashboard.

methodology.evaluation: Seven multi-turn workflow families, 14 held-out rewordings, five OWASP-mapped safety scenarios, 57 recorded voice sessions, tool and grounding review, calibrated answer-quality scoring, and 764 no-cost replay turns retain revisions, denominators, intervals, failures, and fixes.
methodology.boundary: The evaluated Northstar environment uses fictional employee records and application-owned calendar, payroll, benefits, and case services; the capability adapters define where production providers connect.

role: I defined the employee journeys and product architecture; implemented the React, Fastify, shared-contract, workflow, voice, and evidence layers; designed the safety and evaluation program; executed the measured runs; and converted the failure analysis into tested product fixes and a CI release gate.

pageSections.title: Relay turns an employee's intent into a visible, verified workflow
pageSections.description: The employee starts with a question or request. Relay resolves the signed-in employee, reads the relevant records, opens the exact task or document, prepares a registered action, waits for explicit approval, and reports completion only after the application confirms the new state.
pageSections.context: The answer, destination, proposal, confirmation, and resulting record remain visible in one employee workspace.

pageSections.title: A conversational guide operating across the full employee-service workspace
pageSections.markdown:
Relay covers Home, My Onboarding, Tasks, Documents, Learning, Pay & Benefits, Help & Support, meetings, reminders, and workflow operations. The guide opens beside those surfaces on desktop and within a constrained mobile layout, so an employee can move from a spoken or typed request to the source record and resulting action without losing the surrounding application context.

The data model carries the details employees and service teams need to act: status, owner, due health, blocker, employee responsibility, next-step owner, and source condition. Relay reads those typed records before answering. When required data is missing, stale, conflicting, or unavailable, the system returns a typed abstention and a concrete next step instead of inventing a value.

Navigation is semantic and application-controlled. The guide requests a registered route, panel, record, or allowlisted anchor; Relay maps that identifier to the real destination, focuses the matching UI, and checks a visible postcondition. Conversational references such as **Open it** can carry across turns while the application continues to decide which record and destination are valid.

pageSections.title: Application-owned controls turn a request into a trustworthy action
pageSections.description: Each consequential workflow uses the same five-stage contract, giving employees a predictable review step and giving engineering a reusable control plane for identity, authority, retries, audit, and evidence.

items.label: Discover
items.title: Resolve identity and current state
items.body: Bind the session to the signed-in employee and retrieve the relevant scoped records from the server.

items.label: Ground
items.title: Identify the record and responsible path
items.body: Connect the request to a typed source, registered route, responsible party, and permitted next action.

items.label: Prepare
items.title: Inspect the capability and show the proposal
items.body: Run duplicate, ownership, eligibility, and conflict checks, then render the exact proposed write in the workspace.

items.label: Confirm
items.title: Bind approval to the same actor and session
items.body: Wait for the employee to review the visible destination and details, then submit an opaque confirmation token.

items.label: Verify
items.title: Execute once and prove the result
items.body: Use a stable idempotency key, re-read application state, and report success only when the expected record is present.

pageSections.title: Five employee actions share one rigorous execution contract
pageSections.description: Each capability supplies its own eligibility and state-change logic while the shared workflow service supplies actor binding, confirmation, idempotency, ordered audit events, execution receipts, and post-write verification.

items.label: Support
items.title: Create or safely reuse a support case
items.body: Inspect similar cases and the approved service route, prepare a correctly scoped request, and verify that the created or reused case appears in the employee's collection.

items.label: Tasks
items.title: Start an eligible employee task
items.body: Check ownership and current state, transition the task, and re-read the same record to verify that work is in progress.

items.label: Reminders
items.title: Schedule a record-linked reminder
items.body: Validate the referenced task, document, or course and the permitted delay, then create or reuse one reminder with a stable identity.

items.label: Meetings
items.title: Place a conflict-checked meeting
items.body: Resolve an eligible attendee, inspect shared hours and calendar conflicts, keep the draft editable, and add the confirmed meeting with a stable ID.

items.label: Cases
items.title: Add a reviewed case reply once
items.body: Confirm that the case belongs to the employee and remains open, then append the approved response to the same activity history without duplication.

pageSections.title: Success is defined by application state, not preferred wording
pageSections.markdown:
Seven multi-turn development workflows cover onboarding, support, meetings, department routing, pay and benefits, learning and reminders, and service-team calendar coordination. A mobile scenario exercises the same interaction at 390 x 844. Five safety scenarios test private-data disclosure, excessive agency, sensitive input, indirect prompt injection, and false completion claims.

Each live run records the code revision, prompt variant, models, cost, latency, function calls, observable checks, and failure reason. A workflow passes only when every turn reaches the required route, record, confirmation state, calendar state, or server-side result. Fourteen reworded requests stay outside the development loop; any held-out phrase that drives a fix is retired and replaced.

The evaluation program also tests its own measurement tools. Tool scoring checks whether record IDs came from server results and whether the expected record was eventually reached. Grounding review decomposes replies into atomic facts and uses planted errors to measure grader sensitivity. A 100-reply answer-quality sample uses a judge calibrated against human labels. Voice runs measure task outcome, first-audio time, word error rate, key-term recall, and barge-in behavior.

Recurring checks run without paid voice sessions by replaying 764 recorded turns through the real portal and workflow code. CI fails if a live socket opens during replay or if the committed thresholds for task success, safety, factual support, tool use, spoken workflows, answer quality, or interruption handling are missed.

pageSections.title: Conversation, authority, and evidence are separate system responsibilities

items.label: Conversation
items.title: Deepgram carries the real-time turn
items.body: Nova-3 transcribes speech, GPT-4.1 selects functions in the evaluated configuration, and Flux returns audio. The adapter manages playback drain, multi-turn continuity, interruption, reconnect, and inactivity limits.

items.label: Application
items.title: Relay owns identity, policy, and mutation
items.body: Fastify resolves employee scope, validates semantic targets, inspects capability rules, binds confirmation to actor and session, and keeps the long-lived service key behind a short-lived client grant.

items.label: Evidence
items.title: Verified state determines whether a turn passed
items.body: The evaluator checks the visible route, focused record, proposal, confirmation card, calendar, audit chronology, and server records, then retains the run configuration and result for comparison.

pageSections.title: Relay reduces coordination work for employees, service teams, and product engineering

items.label: Employees
items.title: Begin with the need and stay in one workspace
items.body: Employees can ask what is due, inspect the source record, review a proposed action, and see the completed result without learning which portal, queue, form, or owner sits behind the request.

items.label: Service teams
items.title: Receive better-scoped, correctly routed requests
items.body: The capability inspection stage collects required details, chooses a versioned service route, checks duplicates or conflicts, and carries the responsible team and next step into the resulting record.

items.label: Product teams
items.title: Add workflows without expanding model authority
items.body: A new capability implements product-specific inspect and execute behavior while reusing the shared identity, confirmation, idempotency, audit, receipt, and verification lifecycle.

items.label: Engineering
items.title: Replace hand-picked demos with reproducible evidence
items.body: Versioned runs, held-out requests, replay tests, calibrated review, failure categories, and CI thresholds show which behaviors improved and protect them from regression.

pageSections.title: Product design, implementation, evaluation, and iteration formed one body of work
pageSections.markdown: I defined the employee journeys and information architecture; built the React, Fastify, shared TypeScript, workflow, voice, and evidence layers; designed the typed record and capability contracts; implemented confirmation, idempotency, audit, and verification controls; created the live, held-out, replay, safety, grounding, tool, answer-quality, and voice evaluation suites; ran and analyzed the experiments; and converted observed failures into named fixes and an enforced release gate.

pageSections.title: A complete application-owned environment with explicit provider seams
pageSections.markdown:
The evaluated system includes the employee portal, typed employee records, semantic navigation, five confirmation-gated capabilities, calendar and case workflows, reminders, audit state, retained evaluation runs, and live Deepgram voice interaction.

Northstar Analytics and its employee records are fictional, and the calendar, payroll, benefits, case, reminder, and outbox services are application-owned. The adapter contracts identify the integration points for durable HRIS, ticketing, calendar, email, and queue providers.
